newsitem.title: NORWAY: Non-life result weakens Storebrand 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Non-life result weakens Storebrand 1996 profits.

text.p: Storebrand ASA, Norway's biggest insurance company, said on Wednesday that 1996 group profits fell 13.6 percent to 1.25 billion crowns ($179.7 million) partly because of weaker non-life results.
But financial portfolio gains helped offset some of the losses and the result beat market expectations.
The Storebrand Group recorded an operating profit before distribution to the life assurance policyholders of 4.12 billion crowns, or 86 million less than in 1995.
After distributing to the customers their share of the profit from life and pension insurance, the group's profit was 1.25 billion crowns, compared to 1.45 billion in 1995.
The life assurance operation benefited from the positive development in the capital markets in 1996. The operating result was 3.43 billion crowns, up from 3.34 billion in 1995.
For non-life insurance the operating profit was 1.04 billion crowns, down from 1.18 billion.

"This fall was primarily due to the weaker technical result as a consequence, among other things, of an increase in the number of claims referring to damage by fire and water," Storebrand said in a statement.
The earnings per share fell to 4.10 crowns from 4.94 in 1995. The board proposed a dividend of 0.70 crowns per preferential share, unchanged from 1995.
Net gains on the sale of securities totalled 1.68 billion crowns, compared with 964 million in 1995.
Storebrand President and Chief Executive Officer Age Korsvold said the insurer had focused on implementing projects aimed at improving competitiveness in 1996.
"Firstly, these are core processes which will improve the group's non-life insurance operations in such areas as tariffs, underwriting and claims settlement," he said in a statement.
He said gains of more than 200 million crowns had been realised at the end of 1996 as a result of these core projects.

"These gains will be even higher this year and Storebrand maintains its objective of achieving annual gains of between 300 million and 500 million crowns in 1997 as a result of these improvement measures," he said.
"Gains from these projects have made it possible for Storebrand to invest in price cuts and in measures that will contribute to improving competitiveness in the future," Korsvold said.
Furthermore, he noted, the company had started an office streamlining and staff reduction campaign that was expected to save about 250 million crowns this year, he said.
